```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)

evidence_map <- out("figure_s2_2_evidence_map.csv")
panels <- out("figure_s4_study_panels.csv")
manifest <- out("table_s2_1_study_manifest.csv")
table_2 <- out("table_2_ethnicity_meta_regression.csv")
magnitude <- out("text_difference_in_magnitude.csv")

# Fig. S1.1's own plotted values, for entry 9. The published page prints a clipped fragment of
# this estimate, so the corrected side is the maintained figure's own value.
neumark_s1_1 <- out("figure_s1_1_field_ates_forest.csv") |>
  filter(study_name_citation == "Neumark et al. (9): United States")
stopifnot(nrow(neumark_s1_1) == 1)

# Fig. 4's own plotted values, for entry 8. The figure prints no numbers, so the counts the
# entry states are taken from the points the figure actually draws rather than from the data
# behind it: author_classification is the coding, and it is what decides a point's colour.
figure_4 <- out("figure_4_cates_gender_gradient.csv") |> filter(layer == "point")
cells_total <- nrow(figure_4)
cells_imputed <- sum(figure_4$author_classification == "no")
cells_authors <- sum(figure_4$author_classification == "yes")
stopifnot(cells_imputed + cells_authors == cells_total)

# The extraction of the published pages, read for the strings the article itself prints. Every
# other number below is computed from maintained/output/ at the time this document is rendered,
# including the numbers that were not wrong: a token carried over from the published sentence is
# inherited on trust, and rendering the whole sentence from the pipeline is what verifies it.
published <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                      na = character())

paper <- function(id) {
  value <- published$value_paper[published$claim_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

mag <- function(name) {
  value <- magnitude$value[magnitude$quantity == name]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

occupations <- function(id) {
  value <- manifest$n_occupations[manifest$study_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

# A corrected sentence has to read like the published one, so a count the article spells out is
# spelled out here too.
number_word <- function(x) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
             "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
             "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")
  stopifnot(x %in% seq_along(words))
  words[x]
}

continents <- n_distinct(evidence_map$continent)

# The supplement numbers its figures section.index: four figures before section S4, then one
# panel per study, then the gender gradient forest plot and the PRISMA flow diagram.
last_supplementary_figure <- 4 + n_distinct(panels$study_name_citation) + 2

m2_intercept <- table_2 |> filter(model == "Model 2", term == "intercept")
m3_intercept <- table_2 |> filter(model == "Model 3", term == "intercept")

# Entries 12 and 15, both carried rather than corrected. The misspelled study label and the
# signed zero are values in the deposited data rather than anything a rewriting of it
# introduces: the label is a value of study_name_citation, and the two Carlsson rows below are
# zeros whose printed sign is floating-point residue.
ahmed_labels <- panels$study_name_citation |> unique() |> str_subset(fixed("at al.")) |> sort()
carlsson_zero <- panels |>
  filter(study_id == "carlsson_1", occupation_observed == "shop sales assistants")
carlsson_plus <- panels |>
  filter(study_id == "carlsson_1", occupation_observed == "lower secondary teachers (language)")
stopifnot(length(ahmed_labels) == 2, nrow(carlsson_zero) == 1, nrow(carlsson_plus) == 1)
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every correction is defined once, here, and every place that states one
# reads it from this table: the entries below, the reproducibility report's errata table, and
# any later edition, each through errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of this file. The
# alternative is a second hand-typed copy of the same five corrections, which is how a note and
# a README come to disagree about which numbers the article got wrong.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold here,
# something else elsewhere. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be set by
# either.
#
# Numbering is the published note's and is APPEND-ONLY: an entry can already have been cited by
# number, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved, merged or renumbered.
#
# `form` is a later edition's choice of macro for the entry: "full" where the published and
# corrected fields are whole sentences that need setting as blocks, "brief" where the entry is a
# token replacement. It is an editorial judgment about the entry rather than a fact about the
# typesetting, which is why it lives here rather than in a second list.
#
# `location` names where in the published article the corrected passage sits, taken from the
# location column of ground_truth/published_claims.csv for the claim the entry corrects rather
# than read off a page. This document does not print it; a later edition does.
#
# Every corrected number is built with str_glue() from maintained/output/, so it is computed at
# render time rather than typed. The published numbers the article's own pages print are typed,
# except where the extraction already carries them.
#
# `claim_ids` names the ground truth rows the entry corrects, semicolon separated, and it is
# what makes "has this finding been published?" a query over the corpus rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where the entry has no ground truth row, which is the case for a
# reference list, since that is not an extraction claim, and for entry 4, whose claim is
# classed structural in the extraction and so is not required to carry a row. Every id listed
# here is checked against the ground truth by ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R, which refuses
# to finish on a dangling one.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,

  1, "quantity", "extraction", "full",
  "The record spans six continents, not five",
  "published abstract",
  "Since 1983, more than 70 employment audit experiments, carried out in more than 26 countries across [[five]] continents, have randomized the gender of fictitious applicants to measure the extent of hiring discrimination on the basis of gender.",
  str_glue("Since 1983, more than 70 employment audit experiments, carried out in more than 26 countries across [[{number_word(continents)}]] continents, have randomized the gender of fictitious applicants to measure the extent of hiring discrimination on the basis of gender."),
  str_glue(
    "The paper's own evidence map, fig. S2.2, is drawn as {number_word(continents)} continent ",
    "facets: {str_c(sort(unique(evidence_map$continent)), collapse = ', ')}. Section S2 names ",
    "Oceania among the regions where the boom in audit experimentation occurred, and the ",
    "earliest study in the whole record, the Australian one the introduction discusses, is on ",
    "that continent. The sentence describes the wider literature rather than the ",
    "{n_distinct(panels$study_name_citation)} studies reanalysed here, but a superset of those ",
    "studies cannot span fewer continents, so five is too few under any reading."),
  "abstract_continents",

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "Table S2.1 overstates the occupation counts for two studies",
  "published app. table S2.1",
  "Gonzalez et al. (89): Spain ... [[18]] occupations\n\nDahl and Krog (84): Denmark ... [[24]] occupations",
  str_glue("Gonzalez et al. (89): Spain ... [[{occupations('gonzalez_1')}]] occupations\n\nDahl and Krog (84): Denmark ... [[{occupations('dahl_1')}]] occupations"),
  str_glue(
    "The article disagrees with itself in these two rows. Figs. S4.37 and S4.32 plot ",
    "{occupations('gonzalez_1')} and {occupations('dahl_1')} occupations for the same two ",
    "studies, and {occupations('gonzalez_1')} and {occupations('dahl_1')} is what the ",
    "deposited data hold. The other 55 rows of the column are right. The table is not ",
    "reprinted here because its N subjects column cannot be regenerated from the deposit, ",
    "which carries no subject counts."),
  "table_s2_1_occupations",

  3, "typography", "pipeline", "brief",
  "Table 2's Model 2 intercept carries no significance marker",
  "published table 2",
  str_glue(
    "Table 2, Model 2, intercept: −{sprintf('%.2f', abs(m2_intercept$estimate))} ",
    "({sprintf('%.2f', m2_intercept$std.error)}), [[carrying no significance marker]]"),
  str_glue(
    "Table 2, Model 2, intercept: −{sprintf('%.2f', abs(m2_intercept$estimate))} ",
    "({sprintf('%.2f', m2_intercept$std.error)}), [[carrying the two-asterisk marker the ",
    "table's own note gives for P < 0.01]]"),
  str_glue(
    "The Model 2 intercept is printed as −{sprintf('%.2f', abs(m2_intercept$estimate))} with ",
    "no marker, at a p-value of {sprintf('%.5f', m2_intercept$p.value)}. Five decimals rather ",
    "than the three the table's own note uses: at three the p-value reads 0.001, which is the ",
    "threshold for the third star rather than the second, and the correction would be ",
    "ambiguous inside the rule it is being compared against. The numerically identical Model 3 ",
    "intercept, −{sprintf('%.2f', abs(m3_intercept$estimate))}, does carry its two stars. The ",
    "estimate and its standard error are right and only the marker is missing, so what is ",
    "corrected here is the table rather than any sentence."),
  "table_2_model2_intercept_stars",

  4, "cross_reference", "extraction", "full",
  "The article cites a supplementary figure that does not exist",
  "published Design, p. 5",
  str_glue(
    "The PRISMA search process yielded over 70 papers that met our inclusion criteria. Figure ",
    "S6.[[{paper('design_prisma_figure')}]] is a \"PRISMA flow diagram\" that illustrates the ",
    "search strategy and reports the number of records retained at each stage of the process."),
  str_glue(
    "The PRISMA search process yielded over 70 papers that met our inclusion criteria. Figure ",
    "S6.[[{last_supplementary_figure}]] is a \"PRISMA flow diagram\" that illustrates the ",
    "search strategy and reports the number of records retained at each stage of the process."),
  str_glue(
    "The supplementary materials list Figs. S1.1 to S6.{last_supplementary_figure} in their ",
    "front matter, and the PRISMA flow diagram is the last of them. There is no fig. ",
    "S6.{paper('design_prisma_figure')}. The same paragraph cites the evidence map as fig. ",
    "S.2.2, where the figure itself is numbered S2.2."),
  "",

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The difference in the magnitude of the two predicted biases",
  "published Results, p. 6",
  "The magnitude of these biases is higher in women-dominated occupations than in men-dominated occupations, by a statistically significant [[2.10]] points (bootstrapped SE: 0.58), perhaps suggesting that pro--status quo forces operate differently across contexts.",
  str_glue(
    "The magnitude of these biases is higher in women-dominated occupations than in ",
    "men-dominated occupations, by a statistically significant ",
    "[[{sprintf('%.2f', mag('Difference in magnitude'))}]] points (bootstrapped SE: ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', mag('Bootstrapped SE of the difference in magnitude'))}), perhaps ",
    "suggesting that pro--status quo forces operate differently across contexts."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited code and the maintained rewrite both give ",
    "{sprintf('%.5f', mag('Difference in magnitude'))}, which rounds to ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', mag('Difference in magnitude'))} at the two decimal places the sentence ",
    "prints. The published figure is the truncation rather than a different number, and the ",
    "bootstrapped standard error, ",
    "{sprintf('%.4f', mag('Bootstrapped SE of the difference in magnitude'))}, is 0.58 as ",
    "published."),
  "results_magnitude_difference",

  6, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Reference 22 demotes half of an author's surname to an initial",
  "published references, p. 9, and app. references, p. 48",
  "22. M. Carnes, P. G. Devine, [[L. B. Manwell]], A. Byars-Winston, E. Fine, ...",
  "22. M. Carnes, P. G. Devine, L. Baier Manwell, A. Byars-Winston, E. Fine, ...",
  paste("The third author's surname is the compound Baier Manwell, and the entry reads its",
        "first element as a middle initial. Crossref, doi 10.1097/acm.0000000000000552:",
        "Carnes, Molly; Devine, Patricia G.; Baier Manwell, Linda; Byars-Winston, Angela.",
        "PubMed indexes her the same way, as Baier Manwell L."),
  "",

  7, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Reference 65 breaks two surnames beginning \"Mc\"",
  "published references, p. 10, and app. references, p. 52",
  # TWO BLOCKS, because the elision between them is markup rather than text. A
  # later edition's patcher reads "..." as "the quotation opens or closes here"
  # and strips it; an elision left in the MIDDLE of one block is not stripped,
  # and the block then asks the page for a literal "..." that it does not print,
  # so the entry matches nothing and is skipped. Quoting the reference as the
  # two fragments it really is asks for what reference 65 actually sets, and it
  # is also what a reader of this note should see: two names, far apart in a
  # list of twenty-six, with the rest of it elided between them.
  paste0("65. M. J. Page, [[J. E. Mc Kenzie]], P. M. Bossuyt, I. Boutron, ...\n\n",
         "... E. Mayo-Wilson, [[S. M. Donald]], L. A. McGuinness, L. A. Stewart, ..."),
  paste0("65. M. J. Page, J. E. McKenzie, P. M. Bossuyt, I. Boutron, ...\n\n",
         "... E. Mayo-Wilson, S. McDonald, L. A. McGuinness, L. A. Stewart, ..."),
  paste("Joanne E. McKenzie's surname is set with a space, and Steve McDonald's is split so",
        "that its \"Mc\" reads as a middle initial. Crossref, doi 10.1136/bmj.n71: McKenzie,",
        "Joanne E is the second author and McDonald, Steve the nineteenth. The defect is",
        "specific to these two names rather than general to the typesetting: the same entry",
        "sets L. A. McGuinness correctly three names later, and reference 60 sets",
        "M. McPherson correctly."),
  "",

  8, "provenance", "successor_project", "full",
  "Figure 4 colors imputed gender composition categories as though the study authors had given them",
  "published Fig. 4 caption, p. 6",
  paste("The gender composition categories ([[as given by study authors where available and by",
        "us otherwise]]) are distinguished by color and shape (green circles, men-dominated;",
        "orange triangles, gender-balanced; blue squares, [[women-dominated]])."),
  paste("The gender composition categories ([[as given by study authors]]) are distinguished by",
        "color and shape (green circles, men-dominated; orange triangles, gender-balanced; blue",
        "squares, [[women-dominated; grey circles, category not given by the study authors]])."),
  str_glue(
    "Of the {cells_total} study-occupation cells the figure draws, only {cells_authors} carry a ",
    "gender composition category the original study's own authors assigned; the remaining ",
    "{cells_imputed} were filled in by us from where the occupation falls in the ILO gender ",
    "distribution. The caption discloses that in words, so the article is accurate about what it ",
    "did, but the figure gives all {cells_total} points the same three colors, and a color is a ",
    "claim about the occupation that a reader cannot tell apart from the {cells_authors} that ",
    "were coded. The corrected figure draws the {cells_imputed} imputed cells in grey, keeping ",
    "their position, their interval and their weight. NO ESTIMATE MOVES: the meta-regression is ",
    "fitted on the continuous share of women in the occupation and never on the category, so ",
    "Tables 1 and 2, the gender gradient and every study-level effect in the supplementary ",
    "materials are exactly as published. What changes is which of {cells_total} points is which ",
    "color. The coding is the same authors' own, carried back from the successor project, where ",
    "the distinction is kept as a column and the imputed categories are dropped rather than ",
    "plotted."),
  "",

  9, "typography", "extraction", "brief",
  "Figure S1.1 prints a clipped estimate for Neumark et al.",
  "published app. fig. S1.1",
  # The published side comes from the extraction rather than from the pipeline, because the
  # pipeline does not produce it: what the page prints is a fragment of a number no calculation
  # yields. The standard error beside it is the pipeline's, like every other number here.
  str_glue(
    "Fig. S1.1, Neumark et al. (9): United States: ",
    "[[{paper('fig_s1_1_est_neumark_et_al_9_united_states')}]] ",

  str_glue(
    "Fig. S1.1, Neumark et al. (9): United States: ",
    "[[−{sprintf('%.1f', abs(neumark_s1_1$estimate))}]] ",
    "({sprintf('%.1f', neumark_s1_1$std.error)})"),
  str_glue(
    "The figure's own text carries the right number and the page does not print it. Read off ",
    "the glyphs, the row holds exactly 2 . 3 space ( 8 . 4 ) beginning at x0 = 268.50, which ",
    "is where every other three-character value in the column begins, and no minus and no 1 is ",
    "inked anywhere to its left: the short dash that sits there is the row's axis tick, which ",
    "the positive rows carry too. The authors' own field_ates_plot.pdf is the same in both ",
    "respects, so the leading −1 was lost when the figure was drawn rather than when it was ",
    "composed: the label overflows the plot panel and its −1 is clipped out of the ink, while ",
    "the text layer keeps it, which is why pdftotext reports ",
    "−{sprintf('%.1f', abs(neumark_s1_1$estimate))} for a page that shows ",
    "{paper('fig_s1_1_est_neumark_et_al_9_united_states')} and why a token gate cannot see this ",

    "prints it as (−{sprintf('%.1f', abs(neumark_s1_1$estimate))} points, SE: ",

    "−{sprintf('%.6f', abs(neumark_s1_1$estimate))} ",
    "({sprintf('%.6f', neumark_s1_1$std.error)}), so the paper disagrees with itself the way ",
    "entry 2 records for table S2.1. The corrected figure is the maintained pipeline's own, ",
    "which draws the full value: of the 420 words and numbers it carries, 419 are on the ",
    "published page and the one exception is the restored ",
    "−{sprintf('%.1f', abs(neumark_s1_1$estimate))}."),
  "fig_s1_1_est_neumark_et_al_9_united_states",

  # ENTRIES 10 AND 11 ARE ONE FINDING AND NEITHER IS REACHABLE FROM ONE
  # DOCUMENT. The supplementary materials reprint the article's reference list

  # entry by entry, the two printings differ in exactly two places, and they
  # fall on opposite sides: each document is right where the other is wrong.
  # A gate compares an edition against its own published source, so a press
  # that sets one list twice can print it two ways and both comparisons pass at
  # zero unexplained. The second printing is the only instrument that reaches
  # either of these.
  10, "bibliographic", "second_printing", "brief",
  "Reference 9 separates two coauthors with a semicolon",
  "published references, p. 9",
  "9. D. [[Neumark;]] R. J. Bank, K. D. Van Nort, Sex discrimination in restaurant hiring: An audit study. Q. J. Econ. 111, 915–941 (1996).",
  "9. D. Neumark, R. J. Bank, K. D. Van Nort, Sex discrimination in restaurant hiring: An audit study. Q. J. Econ. 111, 915–941 (1996).",
  paste("The entry names three coauthors and separates the first two with a semicolon and the",

        "the other 127 entries in this list separates its authors with commas, and the",

  "",

  paste("Every other entry in both printings of this list numbers itself with a digit and a",

  # THE FIVE ENTRIES BELOW ARE CARRIED, NOT CORRECTED, and that is a call about

  # proposes no change, and its `corrected` column is NA.

  12, "orthography", "authors_archive", "note",

  "Reference 123 misabbreviates Social Indicators Research",
  "published references, p. 11, and app. references, p. 58",
  "... a student sample. [[Soc. Indic.s Res.]] 116, 731–754 (2014).",
  NA_character_,
  paste("The journal is Social Indicators Research, abbreviated Soc. Indic. Res., and the entry",
        "attaches a stray s to the abbreviation of Indicators. Crossref, doi",
        "10.1007/s11205-013-0329-4: Lieselotte Blommaert, Marcel Coenders and Frank van Tubergen,",
        "\"Ethnic Discrimination in Recruitment and Decision Makers' Features\", Social Indicators",
        "Research 116, 731-754 (2014), whose short container title there is Soc Indic Res. Unlike entries 10 and 11, this one is set IDENTICALLY in",
        "both printings of the list, so the second printing reaches it and finds the document",
        "agreeing with itself: what it is wrong against is the journal's name rather than the",
        "volume's other printing. That is what makes it a note here rather than a twelfth",
        "correction, since correcting it would put this edition's two reference lists at odds",
        "with the two the paper published."),
  "",

  # Entry 17 comes from the reference audit's re-run of 2026-10-29. Like entry 16 it is set
  # identically in both printings, but what it is wrong against is a page number the record
  # gives, not a style, so it is corrected in both.
  17, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Reference 83's page range ends one page early, in both printings of the list",
  "published references, p. 10, and app. references, p. 54",
  "Am. J. Sociol. 112, [[1297–1338]] (2007).",
  "Am. J. Sociol. 112, [[1297–1339]] (2007).",
  paste("Crossref, doi 10.1086/511799: Shelley J. Correll, Stephen Benard and In Paik,",
        "\"Getting a Job: Is There a Motherhood Penalty?\", American Journal of Sociology 112,",
        "1297-1339 (2007). The supplementary materials reprint the entry with the same range,",
        "so it is corrected in both places."),
  ""
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))
# form == "note" declares that the entry quotes a passage and proposes no change to it, so it
# has no corrected side. The two have to agree: a note carrying corrected text would print a
# correction this edition does not make, and a correction carrying NA would print "NA" where
# its corrected sentence belongs.
stopifnot(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note"))

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# A field holding two quoted passages keeps them one paragraph apart, and the blockquote has to
# carry the break through as a quoted blank line.
quote_block <- function(x) str_c("> ", str_replace_all(bold(x), "\n\n", "\n>\n> "))

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, hence the leading "\n\n".
emit_entry <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n", quote_block(e$published), sep = "")
  # A note entry has no corrected side, and that absence is the whole of the form: an empty
  # "Corrected:" block would read as a correction to nothing.
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\nCorrected:\n\n", quote_block(e$corrected), sep = "")
  cat("\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists `r number_word(sum(entries$form != "note"))` corrections to "Gender composition predicts gender bias: A meta-reanalysis of hiring discrimination audit experiments," published in *Science Advances* 9, eade7979, doi [10.1126/sciadv.ade7979](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.ade7979): three misstated numbers, one dropped significance marker, one cross-reference to a figure that does not exist, two reference-list entries with an author's name broken, one figure that shows imputed categories as though they had been coded, one supplementary figure that prints an estimate clipped short of its own value, two more reference-list entries, one in each of the two places this paper sets its reference list, and one page range that ends a page early in both. It also carries `r number_word(sum(entries$form == "note"))` entries of a second kind, which quote a passage and propose no change to it: four strings the deposited data supply to the supplement's figures and tables, and one misabbreviated journal name this paper sets identically in both printings of its reference list. **No correction and no note here changes a conclusion of the paper.** The gender gradient, the estimates in Tables 1 and 2, and every study-level effect in the supplementary materials are unaffected.

Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/5MCRNY](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/5MCRNY)) at the time this document is rendered, including the numbers that were not wrong. All but one of the `r number_word(sum(entries$class == "bibliographic"))` reference-list entries are verified instead against the authoritative record at Crossref, named in each entry. The exception, entry 11, is a number that has lost its period, which no external record speaks to: it is verified against the other 127 entries of the list it sits in and against the article's own printing of the same reference. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/galos_coppock_2023](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/galos_coppock_2023).

**Bold marks the corrected token in each corrected sentence.** Entries 3 and 8 correct a table and a figure rather than a sentence, so each is named in the entry and shown in a reprint of the float, which is otherwise identical to the published one. Entry 8's corrected sentence is the figure's own caption, which has to change with it: the caption is the figure's only key, and the published one describes three colors where the corrected figure draws four. Percentage-point quantities are given at the precision the article itself uses for them, which in the Results sentence corrected below is two decimal places. Rounding that sentence to one decimal would erase the correction it needs, since the published and corrected figures differ by a hundredth of a point.

```{r entries-1-2, results="asis"}
walk(c(1, 2), emit_entry)
```

```{r entry-3, results="asis"}
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 3)
cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

**Table 2, corrected.** Meta-regression estimates of the gender gradient by majority/minority status. $^{*}$P < 0.05, $^{**}$P < 0.01, and $^{***}$P < 0.001.

```{r table2}
stars <- function(p) {
  case_when(p < 0.001 ~ "$^{***}$", p < 0.01 ~ "$^{**}$", p < 0.05 ~ "$^{*}$", .default = "")
}

# The article sets its negative numbers with a proper minus sign, so a reprinted table has to
# as well, or it reads as a different typesetting of the same cells.
minus <- function(x) str_replace(x, "^-", "−")

term_labels <- c(intercept = "Intercept", fraction_female = "Gender gradient",
                 ethnicity_fctMajority = "Majority status",
                 `fraction_female:ethnicity_fctMajority` = "Majority $\\times$ gradient")

coefficients <- table_2 |>
  transmute(model,
            term = unname(term_labels[term]),
            estimate = str_c(minus(sprintf("%.2f", estimate)), stars(p.value)),
            std_error = sprintf("(%.2f)", std.error)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(estimate, std_error), names_to = "part", values_to = "cell") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell) |>
  mutate(term = if_else(part == "estimate", term, "")) |>
  select(-part)

footer <- table_2 |>
  distinct(model, tau.squared, nobs) |>
  mutate(Sample = c("Majority status group", "Minority status group", "Both groups"),
         `Tau.squared` = sprintf("%.2f", tau.squared),
         Nobs = as.character(nobs)) |>
  select(model, Sample, `Tau.squared`, Nobs) |>
  pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "term", values_to = "cell") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell)

gg_table <- bind_rows(coefficients, footer) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) replace_na(x, "")))

kable(gg_table, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = "",
      col.names = c("", "Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3"))
```

\parbox{\linewidth}{\footnotesize\raggedright \textit{Note:} The only change from the published table is the marker on the Model 2 intercept. Standard errors in parentheses.}

```{r entries-4-5, results="asis"}
walk(c(4, 5), emit_entry)
```

# The supplementary figure

The entry below is the only one in this note that no comparison of text layers could have found. A figure's label can overflow its plot panel, and what is then clipped away is ink and not text: the page shows one number and its own text layer carries another, so the published figure and any faithful re-extraction of it agree about a value the reader never sees. It was found by reading the two against each other, with an extractor that applies the clipping path and one that does not.

```{r entry-9, results="asis"}
emit_entry(9)
```

# The reference list, set twice

The supplementary materials reprint the article's reference list verbatim, all 128 entries, so this paper sets the same list twice. Diffed entry by entry, the two printings differ in exactly two places, and they fall on opposite sides: each document is right where the other is wrong. Neither defect is reachable from one document alone. A comparison of an edition against its own published source cannot see them, because a press that sets one list twice can print it two ways and both comparisons agree with their own page. The second printing is the instrument here, as a clip-aware reader was for entry 9.

```{r entries-10-11, results="asis"}
walk(c(10, 11), emit_entry)
```

Entry 17 is of a third kind. Both printings set it the same way, so the second printing finds nothing, and what it disagrees with is the page range Crossref records for the article.

```{r entry-17, results="asis"}
emit_entry(17)
```

# Carried, and not corrected

The `r number_word(sum(entries$form == "note"))` entries below are different in kind from the `r number_word(sum(entries$form != "note"))` above. Each quotes a passage this edition reprints exactly as the paper published it, and proposes no change to it.

Four of them are strings the deposited replication archive supplies to the supplement's figures and tables, which print whatever the data hold: a study label misspelled in all eight places the supplement names those two studies, two occupation labels, and a zero whose printed minus sign is floating-point residue rather than a negative estimate. Correcting any of the four on the page would put this edition's floats out of step with the data behind them, and would correct the supplement for a defect that is not the supplement's. The fifth is a journal abbreviation carrying a stray letter, set the same way in both of the two places this paper prints its reference list, so the comparison that found entries 10 and 11 finds this one agreeing with itself.

Each is recorded here because an edition that silently reproduced them would leave a reader unable to tell a faithful reprint from an uncorrected error.

```{r entries-carried, results="asis"}
walk(entries$entry[entries$form == "note"], emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Every other statement
# of these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
